files.evidence: Read in full (406 lines). The only file is resolved beneath workspaceDir with resolveInside (lines 34-44), JSONL parsing errors are logged (226-243), writes are serialized and logged on failure (396-404), LLM content has a fixed yes/no decision sink and bounded pair counts (59-89, 359-382). Prompt manipulation can affect contradiction quality but does not reach a privileged mutation in this module.

Read in full (58 lines). Untrusted memory snippets are escaped and bounded before being wrapped in an explicitly untrusted historical-context block (lines 3-6, 30-54). The silent catch at lines 55-57 is a coding-standard/reliability defect, not a security exploit chain.

Read in full (772 lines). Additive selection is hard-capped (lines 44-53, 341-346), hydrated candidates are capped (415-437), inactive rows are excluded (127-150), and prompt output is escaped/bounded in an untrusted evidence-only block (648-668). The legacy fallback read uses join instead of mandatory resolveInside (59-71), but its root is host-supplied workspaceDir and its suffix is fixed; no attacker-controlled traversal segment or independently privileged sink was established. Hydration catches at 166-168 and 433-435 silently ignore errors and are reliability/policy issues.

Read in full (120 lines). The classifier explicitly recognizes passwords/API keys, bank data, and health data (lines 10-17, 19-37), and buildPushMessage embeds the full card body (lines 85-110). Supporting trace: runClassifier returns that full message in pushMessages (lib/jobs/critical-classifier.js:112-131), and index.js logs the complete result at info level (index.js:3039-3046). This forms a plausible CWE-532 sensitive-data-to-log path. The catch at lines 57-59 is also silent and violates the repository error-handling rule.

Read in full (83 lines). The exported functions interpolate agent directly into join(dir, `${agent}.json`) without safeAgentId or resolveInside (lines 20-27) and then read/write/rename that path (29-55, 70-82). Supporting trace: agent is commandCtx.agentId in the internal classifier command (index.js:2995, 3039). Exploitability depends on whether any in-scope host/adapter can supply a non-canonical agentId, so this remains a candidate for validation rather than a finding. The parse catch at lines 32-36 also fails silently.

rawCandidates.title: Critical-push classification serializes secrets and health data into info logs
rawCandidates.source: Stored memory-card content, including credentials, banking, or health information, enters classifyMemory/buildPushMessage.
rawCandidates.control: Type classification and daily rate limiting control delivery volume but do not redact the body.
rawCandidates.sink: buildPushMessage copies card.text/summary verbatim; runClassifier includes message.text in pushMessages; index.js logs JSON.stringify(result) at info level.
rawCandidates.impact: Anyone with plugin/service log access can recover highly sensitive memory content; the same body is prepared for outbound chat delivery.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Code-level source-to-sink is complete. Validation must establish logger persistence/access, whether the cron result is also delivered despite delivery.mode=none, and whether callers pre-redact card content.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: No attacker-controlled payload is required: storing a credential-like memory and running the enabled classifier is sufficient. Confidentiality impact requires a second principal or compromised component with log/chat access.

rawCandidates.title: Critical-push state path uses an unvalidated agent identifier
rawCandidates.source: Host command context agentId flows to runClassifier.
rawCandidates.control: Fallback to default exists, but there is no safeAgentId or resolveInside check in critical-push-state.
rawCandidates.sink: join(stateDir, `${agent}.json`) is read, written via a temporary sibling, and renamed.
rawCandidates.impact: A traversal-shaped agentId could read and overwrite a JSON-suffixed file outside the critical-push state directory under the service account.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: The unsafe path construction and file sinks are confirmed. Validation must determine whether OpenClaw canonicalizes agentId before commandCtx and whether any chat, plugin, cron, or configuration boundary can supply separators.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires control of commandCtx.agentId (or a direct exported-function caller) plus an execution that increments/saves state; authorized chat args alone do not visibly set agentId.

notes: Two candidates retained for validation; all assigned files were read fully. No feature-disable recommendation is implied: likely remedies are redaction/structured logging and path validation.
